monthly_review.summary: This month shows a marked shift toward higher-intensity running with reduced volume and slower average pace, despite improved aerobic training effect and efficiency.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 effort now dominates your run distribution (35% this month vs 15% last month), indicating a significant strategic shift toward threshold work — but at the cost of aerobic base volume.

goal_tracker.message: You need 39.6 more km across 7 remaining sessions — averaging 5.7 km per session — to match last month's volume. Given your current weekly pattern (e.g., 10 km long run + three ~6 km runs), adding one extra 5–6 km Zone 2 run before month-end is realistic and beneficial for aerobic continuity.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite lower cadence
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved from 13.46 to 13.9 km/hr per bpm, even as cadence dropped from 151 to 148 spm — suggesting longer stride length (75.73–75.77 cm in recent mid-week runs) and reduced ground contact time (305–311 ms) are driving efficiency gains more than turnover.

insights.title: Zone 4 dominance signals intensity creep
insights.body: Zone 4 effort jumped from 15% (last month) to 35% (this month), while Z1+Z2 dropped from 53% to 28% — meaning nearly two-thirds of your time is now spent above aerobic threshold, risking under-recovery and limiting mitochondrial adaptation.

insights.title: Stride length increased, vertical oscillation stable
insights.body: Stride length rose from ~72 cm (June 28) to 75.7–85.3 cm in recent runs, especially during the 10 km (75.73 cm) and easy 4 km (85.27 cm), with vertical oscillation holding steady at 7.6–8.5 cm — indicating form adaptations are supporting pace gains without added bounce cost.

insights.title: Low-HR recovery run underutilized
insights.body: Your 0.9 km run on July 6 had HR=137 bpm (still in Z3) and cadence=149 spm — not truly restorative; meanwhile, your 4.0 km run on July 8 hit HR=129 bpm (solid Z2) but was only 4 km — you’re missing dedicated Z1 recovery sessions (<125 bpm, ≥30 min) that would better support your elevated Z4 load.

recommendations.action: Do a 45-minute Zone 1 run (HR ≤125 bpm) on July 10, prioritizing relaxed breathing and cadence ≥145 spm — no pace target.
recommendations.reason: Your Z1 time dropped to just 13% this month (vs 24% last month), and your lowest HR in recent runs was 129 bpm — a true Z1 session will enhance parasympathetic recovery and capillary density without adding fatigue.

recommendations.action: Repeat your July 5 long run structure (10.0 km at avg HR=166 bpm, pace=8:27/km) but extend first 3 km to Zone 2 (HR 130–138 bpm) before transitioning to Zone 4.
recommendations.reason: This preserves your threshold stimulus while rebuilding aerobic foundation — your Zone 2 time fell from 29% to 15%, and your VO2 max remains stable at 39.0, indicating untapped aerobic reserve.

recommendations.action: Add 2x 30-sec strides (95% effort, full recovery) after your next two Zone 2 runs, focusing on quick turnover (cadence ≥160 spm) and light ground contact (<290 ms).
recommendations.reason: Cadence declined from 151 to 148 spm and your shortest ground contact time was 300 ms (July 8) — strides will reinforce neuromuscular efficiency without cardiovascular stress.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish Zone 1–2 volume as the foundation beneath your growing threshold work — using HR-guided pacing and form cues to protect long-term endurance development and recovery capacity.
suggested_sessions: 10 km progressive: 3 km Z2 → 4 km Z3 → 3 km Z4
